claims.text: In situ TEM can be used to monitor the formation of three-dimensional NM-HEA nanoframeworks.
In situ TEM can control the formation of three-dimensional NM-HEA nanoframeworks.
Real-time TEM insights enable precise atomic control of NM-HEA nanoframework formation.
Real-time TEM insights enable optimization of NM-HEA synthesis conditions.
The initial material is an unstructured noble-metal-based high-entropy-alloy composition.
The proposed intervention is in situ TEM monitoring during NM-HEA nanostructure formation.
The formation procedure involves high-resolution TEM imaging, electron-beam irradiation, and temperature control.
In situ TEM provides real-time monitoring and feedback control of nanostructure formation.
Real-time monitoring and feedback control enable precise control over atomic arrangement.
Precise control over atomic arrangement determines the resulting three-dimensional nanoframework structure.
Using in situ TEM will increase the surface area of NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks by 30% relative to traditional synthesis methods.
Using in situ TEM will enhance catalytic activity by 25% relative to traditional synthesis methods.
The catalytic-activity enhancement corresponds to the predicted increase in surface area.
The exact relationship between in situ TEM monitoring and nanostructure-formation kinetics is not fully understood.
Optimal TEM imaging and electron-beam irradiation parameters for precise atomic control remain undetermined.
